audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 matches a 47.44% win rate over 1895 games: Xerath outranges every tool Galio owns (1050 on Shocking Orb, 1000 on Eye of Destruction, 750 Arcanopulse against a 650 Justice Punch), so the lane is a losing poke war that you leave rather than win.
audit.corrected: Difficulty kept; the level chart was realigned instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: ALL SEVEN chart rows disagreed across layers. full phases[].side read Xerath, Xerath, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill while content win[] read Skill, Galio, Xerath, Xerath, Galio, Xerath, Galio — and every phases[].why was the generic Galio-wins template regardless of the row's verdict.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill/Galio/Xerath/Xerath/Galio/Xerath/Galio — identical to the content layer, so the content layer is right and the full layer is the broken one. The kit supports it: he owns levels 3-5 and the first item on pure range, you own level 6 (a 4000-unit Hero's Entrance against a champion who immobilises himself to ult) and the late game.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[].side moved onto the packet/content verdicts, with matching ratings and rewritten whys, proposed as one atomic group. No win[] edits are needed or possible — the content layer already holds the correct values.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range war — the entire matchup — was never stated in numbers, and Shocking Orb was described only as 'his only CC'.
audit.why: Xerath: Q 750, W 1000, E 1050 (13/12.5/12/11.5/11 — it barely drops with rank), R 5000 and he immobilises himself to fire it. Galio: Q 825, E 650 dash, W 275 taunt, R 4000/4750/5500.
audit.corrected: Trading, cooldowns and Do's now say Q outranges Arcanopulse 825 to 750, that Justice Punch is 650 against 1050 poke, and that his ultimate roots him where your R can land.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d called Shocking Orb a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11 — it is never fifteen seconds, and the fact that it barely shortens with rank is the useful part.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into both fields: Shocking Orb 13s to 11s, Arcanopulse 9s, Shield of Durand 18s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles, grounded in Xerath's ranges and Justice Punch's 11s cooldown.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Worst wave: a hard-shoved wave when your bot lane is fighting — the R you couldn't channel is the fight your team lost. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a middle wave you can leave — Xerath shoves with a 14s Eye of Destruction, so match it and keep the R timer free. Worst wave: a wave held in front of his tower, where you farm inside 1050 poke range for nothing. Crash timing: crash and roam — his lane cannot follow you, and your R covers whatever he snipes.

notes: The full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer on all seven rows; the content layer matched packet.levelChart exactly, so I moved the full layer onto it and rewrote every why and the affected ratings as one atomic group. Separately: the content whys[] array is labelled on a DIFFERENT scale from win[] — whys[0] covers 'level 1-2', whys[1] 'level 3', whys[2] 'level 4', whys[3] 'level 5' — while win[1] is the Level 2 row and win[2] the Level 3 row. So win[1]='Galio' renders next to a whys[1] that says level 3 is Xerath's. I did not touch it because fixing it means re-indexing the whole array, which is not an edit this format can express safely. packet.suspectNames flagged "Use Hero's Entrance" in wants.you[2]; the name is correct as written and was left alone.
